literature.headline_zh: 埃博拉病毒类群本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期埃博拉病毒类群研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 七种化合物显着降低病毒滴度至少 100 倍,且细胞毒性最小,并且 IC 50 值较低。 [10.1016/j.virusres.2026.199823]
历史报告记录了埃博拉病毒病 暴发 期间的重大孕产妇死亡、流产、死产和新生儿 暴发,但大部分证据基于小病例系列、选定的有症状人群和 暴发 特定研究。由于证据基础的异质性,这些风险的程度仍不清楚。 [PMCID:PMC13696912]
该研究揭示了 EBOV-515 交叉反应性的分子基础,并鉴定了 GP 中的几个保守表位,这些表位是交叉反应性抗体的目标。 [10.64898/2026.10.22.761020]

截至 2026 年 8 月 7 日至 8 日,伊图里在 36 个卫生区中的 28 个卫生区报告了 3,636 例确诊病例和 1,551 例死亡(病死率 42.7%),而北基伍在 34 个卫生区中的 12 个报告了 470 例病例和 315 例死亡(病死率 67.0%)。北基伍省的接触者追踪后续行动(74.7%)低于全国数字(79.2%)和 90-95% 的中断阈值。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11126460/v1]
筛选由一位审稿人进行,并由第二位审稿人验证,综合是叙述性的。 [10.17605/osf.io/9jyxk]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Seven compounds significantly reduced virus titers at least 100-fold with minimal cytotoxicity and demonstrated low IC 50 values. [10.1016/j.virusres.2026.199823]

Historical reports have documented significant maternal death, pregnancy loss, stillbirth, and newborn mortality during EVD outbreaks, but much of this evidence is based on small case series, selected symptomatic populations, and outbreak-specific studies. [PMCID:PMC13696912]
The study revealed the molecular basis for EBOV-515 cross-reactivity and identified several conserved epitopes in the GP that are targets for cross-reactive antibodies. [10.64898/2026.10.22.761020]

As of 7–8 August 2026, Ituri reported 3,636 confirmed cases and 1,551 deaths (case fatality 42.7%) across 28 of 36 health zones, while North Kivu reported 470 cases and 315 deaths (case fatality 67.0%) across 12 of 34 health zones. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-11126460/v1]
Screening is by one reviewer with second-reviewer verification, and synthesis is narrative. [10.17605/osf.io/9jyxk]

literature.en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments. Seven compounds significantly reduced virus titers at least 100-fold with minimal cytotoxicity and demonstrated low IC 50 values. [10.1016/j.virusres.2026.199823]. Historical reports have documented significant maternal death, pregnancy loss, stillbirth, and newborn mortality during EVD outbreaks, but much of this evidence is based on small case series, selected symptomatic populations, and outbreak-specific studies. The study revealed the molecular basis for EBOV-515 cross-reactivity and identified several conserved epitopes in the GP that are targets for cross-reactive antibodies. [10.64898/2026.10.22.761020]. As of 7–8 August 2026, Ituri reported 3,636 confirmed cases and 1,551 deaths (case fatality 42.7%) across 28 of 36 health zones, while North Kivu reported 470 cases and 315 deaths (case fatality 67.0%) across 12 of 34 health zones.

news.headline_zh: 埃博拉病毒类群本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期埃博拉病毒类群新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 由本迪布焦病毒引起的埃博拉病毒 暴发,刚果民主共和国报告了确诊病例和死亡病例。暴发 目前是刚果民主共和国有史以来最大的、全球第二大的。联合国儿童基金会将其多部门行动从 60 个卫生区扩大到 63 个,在所有 16 个热点地区保持存在。 [news-67ac08ef5cf9b98e]
据世界卫生组织非洲区域办事处报告,南苏丹进行了一次全面模拟演习,以测试应对本迪布焦病毒病(BVD)的准备情况。 [news-249642ca310c9bd7]
世界卫生组织(WHO)报告称,刚果民主共和国爆发的埃博拉病是由邦迪布古病毒引起的。 [news-bfd05a5b57b8acb0]

模拟演习对于测试这些支柱是否能够以正确的速度和技术准确性协调一致地协同工作,以有效遏制任何潜在的 埃博拉病毒 输入至关重要。”国家公共卫生研究所 (NPHI) 执行主任 Ader Macar Aciek 博士说道,“在模拟演习期间,系统将被激活,包括协调、早期发现、感染预防和控制、病例管理、风险沟通和社区参与以及安全/有尊严的埋葬。”在我们面对病毒本身之前,现在是测试我们 BVD 暴发 遏制能力的时候了。” SIMEX 涉及 10 个参与地点(延比奥 3 个、耶伊 3 个、朱巴 4 个),全部由 9 名协调员、9 名评估员和 9 名观察员提供支持。 [news-a23e9024f7246364]
在冲突和流离失所的情况下,世卫组织加强了对本迪布焦病毒病(BVD)的准备。 [news-ab9b3c2ab006fde3]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Ebola viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: An Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus, with confirmed cases and deaths reported in the DRC. The outbreak is now the largest ever recorded in the DRC and the second largest globally. UNICEF scaled up its multisectoral operations from 60 to 63 health zones, maintaining a presence in all 16 hotspots. [news-67ac08ef5cf9b98e]
South Sudan conducted a full-scale simulation exercise to test readiness for Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), reported by the WHO Regional Office for Africa. [news-249642ca310c9bd7]
Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus was reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). [news-bfd05a5b57b8acb0]

The simulation exercise is critical to test if these pillars can coherently work together at the right speed and technical accuracy to effectively contain any potential Ebola virus importation” Said Dr Ader Macar Aciek, Executive Director, National Public Health Institute (NPHI) “During the simulation exercise, the system will be activated including coordination, early detection, infection prevention and control, case management, risk communication and community engagement and safe/dignified burial.” This is the time to test our capabilities for BVD outbreak containment before we are confronted by the virus itself.” The SIMEX involved 10 participating sites (3 in Yambio, 3 in Yei and 4 in Juba), all supported by 9 facilitators, 9 evaluators and 9 observers. [news-a23e9024f7246364]
WHO scales up readiness for Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) amid conflict and displacement. [news-ab9b3c2ab006fde3]

papers.title: Bundibugyo virus disease in outbreak settings: A practical clinical review
papers.abstract: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe filovirus infection caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an orthoebolavirus with diagnostic and countermeasure implications distinct from Ebola virus (EBOV). The ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has expanded substantially, with 7890 confirmed cases and 3799 deaths reported across 63 health zones in seven provinces as of 23 September 2026. BVD usually presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastrointestinal illness; haemorrhagic manifestations are uncommon at presentation. Early outbreak investigation also showed that EBOV-oriented testing can fail to detect BDBV, making species-appropriate molecular testing essential when BDBV is epidemiologically plausible. Supportive care remains the standard of management, but what can be delivered safely differs between peripheral facilities and dedicated filovirus treatment centres. First-contact facilities should prioritise recognition, separation, protected sampling, treatment of immediately life-threatening or common treatable conditions, and early referral; treatment centres can provide closer monitoring, advanced supportive care, and access to approved research protocols. Insecurity, displacement, laboratory and transport constraints, and delayed presentation continue to limit implementation. No vaccine or specific therapeutic has established clinical efficacy against BDBV in humans; Ervebo is being evaluated within research protocols and the PARTNERS trial is evaluating MBP134 and remdesivir-based regimens. This review synthesises historical and current evidence on recognition, diagnosis, clinical care, infection prevention, referral, and emerging countermeasures in outbreak-affected settings.

papers.title: Identification of small molecule inhibitors of Ebola virus by use of a biologically contained virus system.
papers.abstract: Ebola virus disease is a severe illness with high mortality for which limited therapeutic options are available. Identifying new antiviral drugs that target viral proteins is essential for improving prevention and treatment strategies. In this study, we screened a library of 2,620 small molecules enriched for reported inhibitory activity against cellular and viral helicases to identify phenotypic inhibitors of a biologically contained virus, Ebola∆VP30 virus, in Vero cells stably expressing VP30 protein. Seven compounds significantly reduced virus titers at least 100-fold with minimal cytotoxicity and demonstrated low IC 50 values. Two of these compounds completely inhibited EbolaΔVP30 virus infection, interfering with either virus entry or replication. Although these preliminary screening hits require further optimization and in vivo validation, their identification opens new avenues for anti-Ebola virus drug discovery.

papers.title_zh: 利用生物病毒系统鉴定 埃博拉病毒 的小分子抑制剂。
papers.source_body_en: Ebola virus disease is a severe illness with high mortality for which limited therapeutic options are available. Identifying new antiviral drugs that target viral proteins is essential for improving prevention and treatment strategies. In this study, we screened a library of 2,620 small molecules enriched for reported inhibitory activity against cellular and viral helicases to identify phenotypic inhibitors of a biologically contained virus, Ebola∆VP30 virus, in Vero cells stably expressing VP30 protein. Seven compounds significantly reduced virus titers at least 100-fold with minimal cytotoxicity and demonstrated low IC 50 values. Two of these compounds completely inhibited EbolaΔVP30 virus infection, interfering with either virus entry or replication. Although these preliminary screening hits require further optimization and in vivo validation, their identification opens new avenues for anti-Ebola virus drug discovery.
papers.abstract_zh: 埃博拉病毒病 是一种 死亡率 较高的严重疾病,可用的治疗选择有限。识别针对病毒蛋白的新 抗病毒药物 药物对于改善预防和 治疗 策略至关重要。在这项研究中,我们筛选了一个包含 2,620 个小分子的文库,这些小分子富含报道的针对细胞和病毒解旋酶的抑制活性,以鉴定稳定表达 VP30 蛋白的 Vero 细胞中生物包含的病毒(埃博拉ΔVP30 病毒)的表型抑制剂。七种化合物显着降低病毒滴度至少 100 倍,且细胞毒性最小,并且 IC 50 值较低。其中两种化合物完全抑制埃博拉ΔVP30病毒感染,干扰病毒进入或复制。尽管这些初步筛选的命中需要进一步优化和体内验证,但它们的鉴定为抗 埃博拉病毒 药物发现开辟了新途径。

papers.title: Structure and antigenicity of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein
papers.abstract: An outbreak of ebolavirus disease caused by a new zoonotic spillover of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) is currently spreading at an unprecedented pace in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The outbreak has resulted in 7,733 cases with a case-fatality ratio of 48%, yet no BDBV-specific vaccines or therapeutics are available. The ebolavirus glycoprotein (GP) promotes viral entry and is the target of neutralizing antibodies and vaccine development. Here, we engineered a soluble, prefusion-stabilized GP trimer from a contemporary BDBV isolate and determined its cryo-electron microscopy structure bound to the broadly neutralizing antibody EBOV-515. It reveals the molecular basis for EBOV-515 cross-reactivity and suggests that the antibody inhibits viral entry by interfering with NPC1 engagement in addition to trapping GP in the prefusion conformation and hindering glycan cap cleavage. Mapping lineage-defining substitutions identified changes in GP1 and GP2, including R506S within an antigenic site targeted by multiple broadly neutralizing antibodies recognizing the fusion loop. Nevertheless, we found that several glycan cap-, GP base-, and HR2-directed antibodies cross-reacted and neutralized BDBV DRC/2026 GP pseudovirus with potency comparable or greater to that observed against earlier BDBV isolates and the Zaire ebolavirus Makona/2024 isolate. These findings define the antigenic properties of contemporary BDBV GP and delineate conserved epitopes as ideal targets for antibody therapeutics and for the development of pan-ebolavirus vaccines.

The ebolavirus glycoprotein (GP) promotes viral entry and is the target of neutralizing antibodies and vaccine development. Here, we engineered a soluble, prefusion-stabilized GP trimer from a contemporary BDBV isolate and determined its cryo-electron microscopy structure bound to the broadly neutralizing antibody EBOV-515. It reveals the molecular basis for EBOV-515 cross-reactivity and suggests that the antibody inhibits viral entry by interfering with NPC1 engagement in addition to trapping GP in the prefusion conformation and hindering glycan cap cleavage. Mapping lineage-defining substitutions identified changes in GP1 and GP2, including R506S within an antigenic site targeted by multiple broadly neutralizing antibodies recognizing the fusion loop. Nevertheless, we found that several glycan cap-, GP base-, and HR2-directed antibodies cross-reacted and neutralized BDBV DRC/2026 GP pseudovirus with potency comparable or greater to that observed against earlier BDBV isolates and the Zaire ebolavirus Makona/2024 isolate. These findings define the antigenic properties of contemporary BDBV GP and delineate conserved epitopes as ideal targets for antibody therapeutics and for the development of pan-ebolavirus vaccines.

papers.abstract_zh: 由一种新的人畜共患本迪布焦病毒(BDBV)跨物种溢出引起的埃博拉病毒病暴发目前正在刚果民主共和国和乌干达以前所未有的速度传播。暴发 已导致 7,733 例病例,病死率为 48%,但尚无 BDBV 特异性 疫苗 或治疗方法。埃博拉病毒糖蛋白 (GP) 促进病毒进入,是中和抗体和 疫苗 开发的目标。在这里,我们从当代 BDBV 分离株中设计了一种可溶性、融合前稳定的 GP 三聚体,并确定了其与广泛中和抗体 EBOV-515 结合的冷冻电子显微镜结构。它揭示了 EBOV-515 交叉反应性的分子基础,并表明该抗体除了将 GP 捕获在融合前构象并阻碍聚糖帽裂解之外,还通过干扰 NPC1 接合来抑制病毒进入。谱系定义取代图谱确定了 GP1 和 GP2 的变化,包括识别融合环的多种广泛中和抗体靶向的抗原位点内的 R506S。尽管如此,我们发现几种聚糖帽、GP 碱基和 HR2 定向抗体交叉反应并中和 BDBV DRC/2026 GP 假病毒,其效力与针对早期 BDBV 分离株和扎伊尔埃博拉病毒 Makona/2024 分离株观察到的效力相当或更强。这些发现定义了当代 BDBV GP 的抗原特性,并将保守表位描述为抗体治疗和泛埃博拉病毒 疫苗 开发的理想靶标。

papers.title: Epidemic response performance in contested territory: a comparative analysis of Ituri and North Kivu during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
papers.abstract: Abstract Background. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is unfolding across provinces under materially different governance and security conditions. Ituri, the outbreak's epicentre, remains under national government administration despite insecurity; North Kivu's capital, Goma, and surrounding territory have been under March 23 Movement (M23)/Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) control since early 2025. Existing published accounts treat insecurity as a generic, undifferentiated risk factor rather than isolating the specific contribution of contested territorial control. We compared Ituri and North Kivu on cumulative case fatality, health-zone coverage, and contact-tracing completeness using published, province-disaggregated surveillance figures from WHO, ECDC, and Africa CDC, contextualised against the documented conflict-related disruption of DRC's tenth Ebola outbreak (2018–2020), which affected the same two provinces. Two-proportion z-tests with 95% confidence intervals were used to test whether observed differences exceeded what chance alone would produce; the analysis is presented as hypothesis-generating throughout, consistent with the limits of an ecological design. As of 7–8 August 2026, Ituri had reported 3,636 confirmed cases and 1,551 deaths (case fatality 42.7%) across 28 of 36 health zones; North Kivu had reported 470 cases and 315 deaths (case fatality 67.0%) across 12 of 34 health zones. North Kivu's contact-tracing follow-up (74.7%) fell below both the national figure (79.2%) and the 90–95% interruption threshold. The outbreak reached 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days of response activation, versus approximately 235 days for the 2018 outbreak in the same geography. The study is based on a review of available literature and expert opinion.
analysis.methods: The editorial reviews existing vaccine research and evaluates the potential of vaccine platforms developed for other Ebola viruses, such as Sudan virus and Zaire ebolavirus, to be adapted for Bundibugyo virus. It does not describe specific experimental methods or statistical analyses.
analysis.main_results: The editorial reports that preliminary studies suggest the possibility of using vaccine platforms developed for other Ebola viruses to create efficacious vaccines for Bundibugyo virus. However, no specific results or data are provided in the text.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as a promising avenue for vaccine development against Bundibugyo virus, noting that existing platforms may be applicable. This represents a novel perspective on the potential for cross-virus vaccine strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that vaccine development for Bundibugyo virus could benefit from leveraging existing platforms, which may inform future research and public health strategies for preventing outbreaks of this virus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an editorial review and does not present original data or detailed experimental results. The evidence strength is moderate, as it relies on existing research and expert opinion rather than new findings.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这篇社论讨论了围绕 Bundibugyo 病毒 疫苗 的研究前景,重点关注现有 疫苗 平台的潜力及其对该特定病毒的应用。该研究基于对现有文献和专家意见的回顾。
elements_zh.methods: 该社论回顾了现有的 疫苗 研究,并评估了为其他 埃博拉病毒(例如苏丹病毒和扎伊尔埃博拉病毒)开发的 疫苗 平台适用于本迪布焦病毒的潜力。它没有描述具体的实验方法或统计分析。

papers.title: Filovirus Seroreactivity Beyond Virus-Specific Outbreak Regions in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2015-2023
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is the second-largest Ebola disease outbreak in recorded history, and only the second recorded BVD outbreak in the country. While the DRC has recorded 18 filovirus disease outbreaks, the historical frequency and geographic distribution of human filovirus exposures remain poorly understood. Using a multiplexed multi-filovirus immunoassay, we assessed antibody reactivity against antigens of filoviruses linked to human disease, Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), Ebola virus (EBOV), Marburg virus (MARV), and Sudan virus (SUDV), among eleven cohorts from seven provinces between 2015–2023 (n=5,852). Participants with median fluorescence intensity values exceeding established antigen-specific cutoffs were classified as seroreactive. Seroreactivity against glycoprotein (GP) targets of all four viruses were detected in every cohort, demonstrating evidence of filovirus or an antigenically related exposure well beyond known outbreak regions. Seroreactivity estimates varied by cohort site, with 60.8% of participants (n=175/288) in Mongala Province in April 2016 considered seroreactive against BDBV GP. In this cohort, 4.2%, 29.9%, and 34.7% of participants were seroreactive against EBOV, MARV and SUDV GP, respectively yet only 1.7% were seroreactive against all four GP antigens. In adjusted analyses, site was the primary predictor of seroreactivity, with odds for BDBV seroreactivity 9.1-fold (95%CI 7.0-11.9) and 9.5-fold (95%CI 6.9-13.2) higher in Mongala and Tshuapa provinces than in Kwilu. Similarly, the adjusted odds of MARV and SUDV GP seroreactivity were 4.5-fold and 7.1-fold higher in Mongala, and 3.7-fold and 6.1-fold higher in Tshuapa, than Kwilu. Among 280 individuals sampled longitudinally, BDBV GP detected seroconversion was comparable by site, with 12.8% in Kwilu and 10.4% in Mongala having detected seroreactivity three and five years after initial contact, respectively. Overall, these results indicate widespread, geographically heterogeneous filovirus seroreactivity across sampled cohorts. These findings may reflect zoonotic spillover events, leading to undetected human-to-human filovirus circulation, including paucisymptomatic or asymptomatic infections, or exposure to as-yet unidentified antigenically cross-reactive viruses. These data highlight gaps in understanding the historical and geographic distribution of filovirus exposure in the DRC and support further prospective serological, epidemiological, and molecular investigations, especially given the current outbreak.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 刚果民主共和国(DRC)正在发生的本迪布焦病毒病(BVD)ZX​​QTERMXQXZ是有记录以来第二大埃博拉病毒病暴发,也是该国仅有第二记录的BVD 暴发。尽管刚果民主共和国已记录了 18 种丝状病毒疾病 暴发,但人类丝状病毒暴露的历史频率和地理分布仍知之甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用多重多丝状病毒免疫测定,我们评估了 2015 年至 2023 年间来自七个省的 11 个 队列研究 中与人类疾病相关的丝状病毒、本迪布焦病毒 (BDBV)、埃博拉病毒 (EBOV)、马尔堡病毒 (MARV) 和苏丹病毒 (SUDV) 抗原的抗体反应性 (n=5,852)。
elements_zh.methods: 荧光强度中值超过既定抗原特异性截止值的参与者被归类为血清反应性。血清反应性估计因 队列研究 站点而异,2016 年 4 月蒙加拉省 60.8% 的参与者 (n=175/288) 被认为对 BDBV GP 有血清反应性。在该 队列研究 中,分别有 4.2%、29.9% 和 34.7% 的参与者对 EBOV、MARV 和 SUDV GP 呈血清反应,但只有 1.7% 对所有四种 GP 抗原呈血清反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 在每个 队列研究 中均检测到所有四种病毒针对糖蛋白 (GP) 靶标的血清反应性,证明丝状病毒或抗原相关暴露的证据远远超出已知的 暴发 区域。在调整后的分析中,地点是血清反应性的主要预测因素,蒙加拉省和楚阿帕省的 BDBV 血清反应性几率比奎卢省高 9.1 倍(95% CI 7.0-11.9)和 9.5 倍(95% CI 6.9-13.2)。同样,Mongala 地区 MARV 和 SUDV GP 血清反应性的调整后赔率比 Kwilu 地区高 4.5 倍和 7.1 倍,Tshuapa 地区高 3.7 倍和 6.1 倍。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现可能反映了人畜共患的 跨物种溢出 事件,导致未检测到的人际丝状病毒传播,包括少症状或无症状感染,或暴露于尚未鉴定的抗原交叉反应病毒。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明 队列研究 样本中存在广泛的、地理异质的丝状病毒血清反应性。这些数据凸显了在了解刚果民主共和国丝状病毒暴露的历史和地理分布方面的差距,并支持进一步的前瞻性血清学、流行病学和分子研究,特别是考虑到当前的 暴发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据没有报告任何随机化或盲法,这可能会引入偏差。研究设计的局限性和缺乏比较组降低了证据的强度。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现可能反映了人畜共患的 跨物种溢出 事件,导致未检测到的人际丝状病毒传播,包括少症状或无症状感染,或暴露于尚未鉴定的抗原交叉反应病毒。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明 队列研究 样本中存在广泛的、地理异质的丝状病毒血清反应性。这些数据凸显了在了解刚果民主共和国丝状病毒暴露的历史和地理分布方面的差距,并支持进一步的前瞻性血清学、流行病学和分子研究,特别是考虑到当前的 暴发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据没有报告任何随机化或盲法,这可能会引入偏差。研究设计的局限性和缺乏比较组降低了证据的强度。

papers.title: Bundibugyo virus disease and military health facilities in Nigeria: a rapid review of clinical, diagnostic and countermeasure evidence and surveillance integration gaps.
papers.abstract: This project is a rapid review of the evidence on Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) and its implications for military health facilities in Nigeria. Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) caused the largest Ebola disease epidemic ever recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May 2026, with onward cases in Uganda, Kenya, Europe and, on 20 October 2026, an imported case in Abuja, Nigeria. Ebola preparedness across Africa was built around a different species, Zaire ebolavirus: the licensed vaccine, the licensed monoclonal antibody therapies and the most widely deployed near-patient diagnostic assay all target that species, and none is approved for BDBV. The review has two purposes. The first is to consolidate current evidence on BDBV virology, clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, vaccines and infection prevention, as of late October 2026. The second is to examine how Nigerian military health facilities connect to the national Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) system. These facilities serve internationally deployed personnel, their families and often civilian patients, but report through a separate command chain, and no published study has measured their surveillance reporting. Methods follow Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group guidance, reported using PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. Searches of PubMed, Europe PMC, HAL, African Journals Online and ClinicalTrials.gov were run on 24 October 2026, supplemented by WHO, Africa CDC, ECDC, US CDC, Nigerian government and United Nations sources. Screening is by one reviewer with second-reviewer verification, and synthesis is narrative. Expected outcomes are a current synthesis of BDBV evidence for clinicians and public health staff in West Africa, a description of how military health facilities sit relative to national surveillance in Nigeria, and a set of preparedness priorities for those facilities covering surveillance connection, screening of returning personnel, case definitions, laboratory pathways, isolation readiness, joint contact tracing and trial access. A further expected outcome is documentation of an evidence gap: preliminary searching found no study measuring IDSR reporting from Nigerian military facilities. If confirmed, that absence is itself a finding, and the review will propose a facility-level assessment as the priority next study. The search strategy, record list, screening decisions and literature matrix will be deposited with this project. The protocol was registered after the searches and a first pass of title and abstract screening, but before full-text screening, data extraction and synthesis; no protocol was registered prospectively.

Searches of PubMed, Europe PMC, HAL, African Journals Online and ClinicalTrials.gov were run on 24 October 2026, supplemented by WHO, Africa CDC, ECDC, US CDC, Nigerian government and United Nations sources. papers.full_text: BackgroundEbola virus disease (EVD) is a severe viral infection that can substantially affect maternal and neonatal health through both direct disease and disruption of essential health services. Pregnant women and neonates may experience serious adverse outcomes during outbreaks, yet pregnancy-specific evidence remains limited and maternal–neonatal health has historically received insufficient attention in Ebola preparedness and research.MethodsThis narrative review synthesized evidence on Ebola virus disease and maternal–neonatal health from peer-reviewed literature, international guidance, and outbreak reports. Relevant literature was identified through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar and through reference-list screening of key publications. Findings were synthesized narratively, with attention to study design, methodological limitations, and differences across outbreak settings.FindingsAvailable evidence indicates that EVD during pregnancy is associated with severe maternal complications and poor fetal and neonatal outcomes, although risk estimates remain uncertain because of small and heterogeneous studies. Placental infection and mother-to-child transmission have been documented. Ebola outbreaks also disrupt antenatal, delivery, immunization, and emergency obstetric services, contributing to additional maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. Key preparedness gaps include limited maternity-specific IPC, inadequate pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance, and insufficient evidence on vaccines and therapeutics in pregnancy.ConclusionEVD poses serious but context-dependent risks to maternal and neonatal health through direct disease and disruption of essential healthcare services. Preparedness should prioritize continuity of essential maternity and newborn care, maternity-specific IPC, pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance, and the responsible inclusion of pregnant and breastfeeding women in vaccine and therapeutic research and access. 2Methodology2.1OverviewThis study employed a narrative review methodology guided by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) to enhance transparency, methodological rigor, and critical synthesis. The review examined the direct and indirect effects of Ebola virus disease (EVD) on maternal and neonatal health, including clinical outcomes, health-service disruption, and preparedness gaps. A narrative approach was appropriate because the available evidence includes heterogeneous observational studies, outbreak reports, case series, modeling studies, reviews, and public-health guidance.2.1.1Literature identification and selectionRelevant literature was identified through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, together with examination of the reference lists of key reviews and primary studies. Searches focused on combinations of terms related to Ebola virus disease, pregnancy, maternal health, fetal and neonatal outcomes, vertical transmission, infection prevention and control, health-service disruption, vaccination, therapeutics, surveillance, and preparedness.The purpose of the search was to identify literature relevant to the objectives of this narrative review rather than to conduct an exhaustive or systematic search of all available evidence. Publications were selected on the basis of their relevance to maternal, fetal, neonatal, placental, and health-system aspects of Ebola virus disease. Because this was a narrative review, a formal systematic-review protocol, PRISMA-based screening process, and database-specific reproducible search strategy were not applied.2.1.2Inclusion and exclusion criteriaPublications were included if they reported maternal, fetal, neonatal, placental, or pregnancy-related outcomes associated with EVD; examined disruption of maternal and child health services; or addressed outbreak preparedness, IPC, surveillance, vaccination, or therapeutics. Relevant observational studies, outbreak investigations, case reports/series, modeling studies, reviews, and authoritative public-health guidance were considered.Publications were excluded if they were duplicates, outside the specified period, unavailable in English, unrelated to maternal–neonatal health, or lacked sufficient substantive information for interpretation.2.1.3Data extraction and synthesisRelevant information was extracted according to major themes: EVD epidemiology in pregnancy, maternal vulnerability, placental and vertical transmission, maternal outcomes, fetal and neonatal outcomes, disruption of maternal and child health services, and health-system preparedness.Because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, outbreak settings, sample sizes, and reported outcomes, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate. Findings were therefore synthesized narratively through thematic comparison, with emphasis on consistent patterns, conflicting evidence, contextual differences, and remaining knowledge gaps.2.1.4Quality assessment of sourcesThe overall quality and reporting of the review were guided by SANRA principles. Included evidence was critically evaluated according to study design, outbreak setting, sample size, population definition, case definition, outcome ascertainment, availability of comparison groups, and whether estimates were directly observed or model-derived.No single formal risk-of-bias tool was applied because of the substantial heterogeneity of the evidence base. Greater interpretive weight was given to studies with clearly defined populations, transparent denominators, appropriate comparison groups, and well-documented outcomes, while small case series, historical reports, and model-based estimates were interpreted cautiously. 11DiscussionThis narrative review focuses on the complex link between EVD and maternal and neonatal health. According to available information, pregnancies complicated by symptomatic maternal EVD can result in catastrophic maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes, whereas Ebola epidemics can interrupt critical reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health services at the same time.The existing evidence suggests a link between symptomatic maternal EVD and substantial poor pregnancy outcomes, but the extent of these risks is unclear. Historical reports have reported significant maternal death, pregnancy loss, stillbirth, and newborn mortality; however, much of this information is based on tiny case series, selected symptomatic populations, and outbreak-specific studies. As a result, previous estimates should not be taken as universal risks that apply to all pregnant women with Ebola virus infection.Placental involvement has been documented in pregnancies affected by maternal EVD and may contribute to adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes (5, 6, 11, 12). Nevertheless, maternal EVD, placental infection, fetal infection, vertical transmission, and neonatal infection represent distinct clinical and biological phenomena. The relative contributions of placental infection, severe maternal systemic illness, gestational timing, and other clinical factors to specific pregnancy outcomes remain incompletely characterized.An equally noteworthy result is the significant indirect burden associated with health-care disruption. Observational studies conducted during the 2014–2016 West African epidemic revealed declines in antenatal care, facility-based delivery, skilled birth attendance, children immunization, and other critical services (7–9). Modeling studies have indicated higher maternal and neonatal mortality and stillbirth rates associated with decreased healthcare utilization. However, these mortality estimates are model-derived and context sensitive, and should not be taken as proving that indirect mortality always equals or exceeds mortality directly attributed to EVD.The interpretation of pregnancy-associated EVD outcomes must take into account significant variation among outbreaks. Differences in viral species, outbreak magnitude and length, baseline health-system capability, surveillance quality, supportive and obstetric care availability, and vaccine and treatment access may all have an impact on reported maternal and neonatal outcomes. Findings from previous outbreaks and the 2014–2016 West African epidemic should not be applied to future outbreaks or different healthcare settings.The study also shows that pregnant women and newborns face continuous readiness issues. Maternity services necessitate IPC procedures that allow for obstetric exposure to potentially infected bodily fluids while maintaining availability to emergency care. Pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance remains critical for producing accurate estimates of maternal and neonatal outcomes. At the same time, limited pregnancy-specific vaccine and therapeutic evidence continues to constrain evidence-based decision-making.These findings support a preparedness approach that integrates maternal and neonatal health into outbreak response rather than treating maternity services as secondary to pathogen-control activities. The recommendations proposed in this review including strengthening pregnancy-specific surveillance, maintaining maternity-specific IPC and service continuity, and supporting responsible inclusion in vaccine and therapeutic research represent priorities derived from the overall narrative synthesis rather than direct empirical findings from any single study. 15ConclusionAvailable evidence suggests that pregnancies complicated by symptomatic EVD pose significant maternal, fetal, and neonatal risks; however, the magnitude of these risks varies across outbreaks and is unknown due to small sample sizes, heterogeneous evidence, differences in clinical management, and limited pregnancy-specific surveillance.National authorities, regulators, research sponsors, ethics committees, and international health organizations should avoid automatic exclusion of pregnant and breastfeeding women from potentially beneficial Ebola interventions and research. Decisions should be based on assessment of intervention-specific risks and benefits, disease severity, available evidence, and ethical considerations. Pregnancy-specific pharmacovigilance and maternal–infant outcome monitoring should accompany vaccine and therapeutic deployment whenever feasible.Pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance, continuity of key maternity and newborn services, maternity-specific IPC readiness, and responsible access to vaccinations and medicines should all be integrated into overall outbreak planning and response. Since its first outbreaks were identified in 1976, EVD has caused recurrent epidemics, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa, with case fatality rates ranging from roughly 25 to 90% depending on viral species, outbreak characteristics, and healthcare capacity (1–3). Despite this vulnerability, pregnant women have historically been underrepresented.The 2014–2016 West African Ebola epidemic marked a watershed moment in understanding the effects of EVD on maternal and newborn populations. “Although symptomatic maternal EVD was associated with serious adverse outcomes, the epidemic also demonstrated the substantial indirect effects of health-system disruption.” Fear of Ebola transmission, healthcare worker infections, and resource reallocation all contributed to lower rates of prenatal care attendance, skilled birth attendance, emergency obstetric services, and childhood vaccine coverage (7–9). This integrated approach provides a broader basis for identifying priorities for protecting pregnant women and newborns during future Ebola outbreaks.As a result, the purpose of this narrative review is to critically synthesize current evidence on the direct and indirect effects of EVD on maternal and neonatal health, identify significant gaps in outbreak preparedness and pregnancy-specific evidence, and highlight priorities for improving maternal and neonatal health protection during future Ebola outbreaks (Figure 1).Figure 1Conceptual framework illustrating the direct and indirect pathways through which Ebola virus disease may affect maternal and neonatal health.Opportunistic Strategic Framework matrix graphic with two axes: adaptability (low to high) and impact (low to high). Findings from previous outbreaks and the 2014–2016 West African epidemic should not be applied to future outbreaks or different healthcare settings.The study also shows that pregnant women and newborns face continuous readiness issues. Maternity services necessitate IPC procedures that allow for obstetric exposure to potentially infected bodily fluids while maintaining availability to emergency care. Pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance remains critical for producing accurate estimates of maternal and neonatal outcomes. At the same time, limited pregnancy-specific vaccine and therapeutic evidence continues to constrain evidence-based decision-making.These findings support a preparedness approach that integrates maternal and neonatal health into outbreak response rather than treating maternity services as secondary to pathogen-control activities. The recommendations proposed in this review including strengthening pregnancy-specific surveillance, maintaining maternity-specific IPC and service continuity, and supporting responsible inclusion in vaccine and therapeutic research represent priorities derived from the overall narrative synthesis rather than direct empirical findings from any single study.
full_text_sections.conclusion: 15ConclusionAvailable evidence suggests that pregnancies complicated by symptomatic EVD pose significant maternal, fetal, and neonatal risks; however, the magnitude of these risks varies across outbreaks and is unknown due to small sample sizes, heterogeneous evidence, differences in clinical management, and limited pregnancy-specific surveillance.National authorities, regulators, research sponsors, ethics committees, and international health organizations should avoid automatic exclusion of pregnant and breastfeeding women from potentially beneficial Ebola interventions and research. Decisions should be based on assessment of intervention-specific risks and benefits, disease severity, available evidence, and ethical considerations. Pregnancy-specific pharmacovigilance and maternal–infant outcome monitoring should accompany vaccine and therapeutic deployment whenever feasible.Pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance, continuity of key maternity and newborn services, maternity-specific IPC readiness, and responsible access to vaccinations and medicines should all be integrated into overall outbreak planning and response. Strengthening the knowledge foundation through pregnancy-specific research and maternal–infant follow-up will also help to improve clinical and public-health decision-making during future epidemics.
full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionOne of the deadliest infectious diseases affecting human populations, Ebola virus disease (EVD) is caused by viruses that belong to the Ebolavirus genus. Since its first outbreaks were identified in 1976, EVD has caused recurrent epidemics, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa, with case fatality rates ranging from roughly 25 to 90% depending on viral species, outbreak characteristics, and healthcare capacity (1–3). In addition to the high mortality among infected individuals, Ebola outbreaks often overburden vulnerabilities in global health preparedness (1, 3, 4).Pregnant women and newborns are a particularly vulnerable population during Ebola outbreaks because of the complex physiological and immunological adaptations that may influence host responses to severe viral infections, and maternity care environments involve frequent exposure to blood and body fluids, creating unique infection prevention challenges for healthcare workers (5, 6). Despite this vulnerability, pregnant women have historically been underrepresented.The 2014–2016 West African Ebola epidemic marked a watershed moment in understanding the effects of EVD on maternal and newborn populations. “Although symptomatic maternal EVD was associated with serious adverse outcomes, the epidemic also demonstrated the substantial indirect effects of health-system disruption.” Fear of Ebola transmission, healthcare worker infections, and resource reallocation all contributed to lower rates of prenatal care attendance, skilled birth attendance, emergency obstetric services, and childhood vaccine coverage (7–9). These indirect repercussions demonstrated that Ebola’s impact goes beyond viral transmission to encompass broader shortcomings in maintaining key health services during emergencies.Previous reviews have addressed important but relatively distinct aspects of EVD in pregnancy. Jamieson et al. focused primarily on the clinical and obstetric management of pregnant women with EVD and the occupational risks associated with maternity care, whereas Kourtis et al. emphasized pregnancy-specific clinical considerations and infection prevention and control. Bebell et al. subsequently synthesized published evidence on maternal and perinatal outcomes, including pregnancy loss, neonatal outcomes, and placental involvement. However, these reviews were largely based on small case series, historical outbreak reports, and limited pregnancy-specific data, and they focused predominantly on the direct clinical consequences of maternal EVD. The indirect effects of Ebola outbreaks on maternal and newborn health services, together with preparedness issues such as maternity-specific IPC, pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance, vaccination, therapeutics, and continuity of essential obstetric and neonatal care, have generally been considered separately. The present review addresses this gap by integrating direct maternal, fetal, and neonatal consequences with indirect health-system effects and preparedness deficiencies within a single maternal–neonatal health framework. This integrated approach provides a broader basis for identifying priorities for protecting pregnant women and newborns during future Ebola outbreaks.As a result, the purpose of this narrative review is to critically synthesize current evidence on the direct and indirect effects of EVD on maternal and neonatal health, identify significant gaps in outbreak preparedness and pregnancy-specific evidence, and highlight priorities for improving maternal and neonatal health protection during future Ebola outbreaks (Figure 1).Figure 1Conceptual framework illustrating the direct and indirect pathways through which Ebola virus disease may affect maternal and neonatal health.Opportunistic Strategic Framework matrix graphic with two axes: adaptability (low to high) and impact (low to high). High impact with low adaptability suggests refining core processes; high impact with high adaptability recommends driving strategic innovation. Low impact and low adaptability involve exploring new opportunities, while low impact and high adaptability focuses on eliminating obsolete practices. 2.1OverviewThis study employed a narrative review methodology guided by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) to enhance transparency, methodological rigor, and critical synthesis. The review examined the direct and indirect effects of Ebola virus disease (EVD) on maternal and neonatal health, including clinical outcomes, health-service disruption, and preparedness gaps. A narrative approach was appropriate because the available evidence includes heterogeneous observational studies, outbreak reports, case series, modeling studies, reviews, and public-health guidance.2.1.1Literature identification and selectionRelevant literature was identified through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, together with examination of the reference lists of key reviews and primary studies. Searches focused on combinations of terms related to Ebola virus disease, pregnancy, maternal health, fetal and neonatal outcomes, vertical transmission, infection prevention and control, health-service disruption, vaccination, therapeutics, surveillance, and preparedness.The purpose of the search was to identify literature relevant to the objectives of this narrative review rather than to conduct an exhaustive or systematic search of all available evidence. Publications were selected on the basis of their relevance to maternal, fetal, neonatal, placental, and health-system aspects of Ebola virus disease. Because this was a narrative review, a formal systematic-review protocol, PRISMA-based screening process, and database-specific reproducible search strategy were not applied.2.1.2Inclusion and exclusion criteriaPublications were included if they reported maternal, fetal, neonatal, placental, or pregnancy-related outcomes associated with EVD; examined disruption of maternal and child health services; or addressed outbreak preparedness, IPC, surveillance, vaccination, or therapeutics. Relevant observational studies, outbreak investigations, case reports/series, modeling studies, reviews, and authoritative public-health guidance were considered.Publications were excluded if they were duplicates, outside the specified period, unavailable in English, unrelated to maternal–neonatal health, or lacked sufficient substantive information for interpretation.2.1.3Data extraction and synthesisRelevant information was extracted according to major themes: EVD epidemiology in pregnancy, maternal vulnerability, placental and vertical transmission, maternal outcomes, fetal and neonatal outcomes, disruption of maternal and child health services, and health-system preparedness.Because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, outbreak settings, sample sizes, and reported outcomes, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate. Findings were therefore synthesized narratively through thematic comparison, with emphasis on consistent patterns, conflicting evidence, contextual differences, and remaining knowledge gaps.2.1.4Quality assessment of sourcesThe overall quality and reporting of the review were guided by SANRA principles. papers.title_original: Ebola virus disease and maternal–neonatal health: direct and indirect impacts and health system preparedness gaps

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore the direct and indirect impacts of Ebola virus disease on maternal–neonatal health and identify gaps in health system preparedness. The background highlights the recurring epidemics of EVD in sub-Saharan Africa and the associated high case fatality rates, emphasizing the need for targeted research on maternal and neonatal outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A narrative review was conducted using a comprehensive search strategy across PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, focusing on literature related to EVD, maternal health, fetal and neonatal outcomes, and health system preparedness. The study included observational studies, outbreak reports, case series, modeling studies, and public-health guidance.
analysis.methods: The review employed a narrative approach without a formal systematic-review protocol or PRISMA-based screening process. Literature was identified through targeted searches and reference lists, and publications were selected based on their relevance to maternal, fetal, neonatal, placental, or pregnancy-related outcomes associated with EVD. Data were synthesized narratively through thematic comparison, with emphasis on consistent patterns and knowledge gaps.
analysis.main_results: Historical reports have documented significant maternal death, pregnancy loss, stillbirth, and newborn mortality during EVD outbreaks, but much of this evidence is based on small case series, selected symptomatic populations, and outbreak-specific studies. The extent of these risks remains unclear due to the heterogeneity of the evidence base.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that pregnancies complicated by symptomatic EVD are associated with substantial risks, but the magnitude of these risks is not well understood. The novelty lies in highlighting the need for more focused research and surveillance on maternal–neonatal health during EVD outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of integrating pregnancy-specific pharmacovigilance and maternal–infant outcome monitoring into outbreak planning and response. They also emphasize the need for continuity of maternity and newborn services and improved preparedness for maternal–neonatal health during EVD outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the small sample sizes, heterogeneous evidence, and differences in clinical management across outbreaks. The evidence strength is moderate, as findings are based on narrative synthesis rather than quantitative analysis, and the data are primarily derived from observational studies and outbreak reports.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a narrative review to examine the direct and indirect impacts of Ebola virus disease (EVD) on maternal–neonatal health and identify gaps in health system preparedness. The review focused on literature related to EVD, maternal health, fetal and neonatal outcomes, and health system responses, synthesizing findings through thematic comparison. The results indicate that pregnancies complicated by symptomatic EVD are associated with significant risks, including maternal death, pregnancy loss, stillbirth, and newborn mortality, though much of the evidence is based on small case series and outbreak-specific studies. The authors interpret that these risks are substantial but not fully quantified, emphasizing the need for more targeted research and surveillance on maternal–neonatal health during EVD outbreaks. The study highlights the importance of integrating pregnancy-specific monitoring into outbreak planning and response. However, the evidence is limited by the heterogeneity of the data and the lack of large-scale, standardized studies, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨 埃博拉病毒病 对孕产妇-新生儿健康的直接和间接影响,并找出卫生系统准备方面的差距。这一背景凸显了埃博拉病毒病在撒哈拉以南非洲地区反复流行以及相关的高病死率,强调需要对孕产妇和新生儿结局进行有针对性的研究。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 PubMed、Scopus 和 Google Scholar 的综合搜索策略进行叙述性综述,重点关注与埃博拉病毒病、孕产妇健康、胎儿和新生儿结局以及卫生系统准备情况相关的文献。该研究包括观察性研究、暴发 报告、病例系列、模型研究和公共卫生指导。
elements_zh.methods: 该评价采用叙述性方法,没有正式的系统评价方案或基于 PRISMA 的筛选过程。通过有针对性的搜索和参考列表确定文献,并根据其与埃博拉病毒病相关孕产妇、胎儿、新生儿、胎盘或妊娠相关结局的相关性选择出版物。通过主题比较以叙述方式综合数据,强调一致的模式和知识差距。
elements_zh.main_results: 历史报告记录了埃博拉病毒病 暴发 期间的重大孕产妇死亡、流产、死产和新生儿 暴发,但大部分证据基于小病例系列、选定的有症状人群和 暴发 特定研究。由于证据基础的异质性,这些风险的程度仍不清楚。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,妊娠并发有症状的埃博拉病毒病与重大风险相关,但这些风险的严重程度尚不清楚。新颖之处在于强调需要对埃博拉病毒病期间的孕产妇-新生儿健康进行更有针对性的研究和监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了将妊娠特异性药物警戒和母婴结局监测纳入 暴发 规划和应对的重要性。他们还强调,需要在埃博拉病毒病 暴发 期间保持孕产妇和新生儿服务的连续性,并改善孕产妇和新生儿健康的准备工作。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量小、证据异构以及 暴发 临床管理差异的限制。证据强度中等,因为研究结果基于叙述综合而不是定量分析,并且数据主要来自观察性研究和 暴发 报告。

papers.title: Immunologic and placental responses to the VSV-EBOV vaccine in a pregnant mouse model.
papers.abstract: Ebola virus disease is a severe viral hemorrhagic illness with high maternal and perinatal mortality. Although the replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus-based Ebola vaccine (VSV-EBOV) has been deployed successfully in outbreak settings, pregnant women were excluded from clinical trials, leaving critical safety gaps. To address this, we developed a murine model to assess pregnancy outcomes following VSV-EBOV exposure at different gestational stages. Pregnant C57BL/6 mice vaccinated at embryonic day 7 (E7), E10, or E15 mounted robust anti-Ebola virus (anti-EBOV) antibody responses comparable to those of non-pregnant controls and efficiently cleared the vaccine virus without evidence of vertical transmission. However, peri-implantation vaccination modestly increased fetal resorption and early postnatal mortality, accompanied by placental pathology characterized by vascular remodeling defects and inflammation. Later gestational vaccination had minimal impact on survival or offspring development. Mechanistic studies revealed that these adverse effects were mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection, as IFN-β-deficient mice exhibited normal pregnancy outcomes and blocking interferon receptor activity ameliorated placental pathology despite higher viral loads. To our knowledge, these findings represent the first comprehensive preclinical safety evaluation of VSV-EBOV vaccination during pregnancy and identify a critical window of vulnerability early in gestation. More broadly, this work underscores the central role of interferons in shaping placental immune responses and provides an experimental framework to guide evaluation of live-virus vaccines in pregnancy.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the safety and immunologic responses of the VSV-EBOV vaccine in a pregnant mouse model. The research addresses the critical safety gaps in vaccine trials for pregnant women, as they were excluded from clinical studies. Using a murine model, the study evaluates pregnancy outcomes following vaccination at different gestational stages. Results show that vaccination during early pregnancy leads to increased fetal resorption and placental pathology, while later vaccination has minimal impact. Mechanistic studies suggest that these effects are mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection. The findings provide important insights into the safety of live-virus vaccines during pregnancy and highlight the role of interferons in placental immune responses. The study's results are based on direct observations in a controlled experimental setting, offering a preclinical framework for future research. However, the study is limited to a murine model, which may not fully translate to human outcomes.

papers.abstract_zh: 埃博拉病毒病 是一种严重的病毒性出血性疾病,孕产妇和围产儿 死亡率 发病率较高。尽管基于水泡性口炎病毒的埃博拉 疫苗 (VSV-EBOV) 已在 暴发 环境中成功部署,但孕妇被排除在临床试验之外,从而留下了严重的安全漏洞。为了解决这个问题,我们开发了一种小鼠模型来评估不同妊娠阶段暴露于 VSV-EBOV 后的妊娠结局。在胚胎第 7 天 (E7)、E10 或 E15 接种疫苗的怀孕 C57BL/6 小鼠产生了与非怀孕对照相当的强大抗 埃博拉病毒(抗 EBOV)抗体反应,并有效清除了 疫苗 病毒,而没有垂直 传播 的证据。然而,围植入期 疫苗接种 适度增加胎儿吸收和产后早期 死亡率,并伴有以血管重塑缺陷和炎症为特征的胎盘病理。妊娠后期 疫苗接种 对生存或后代发育的影响很小。机制研究表明,这些不良反应是由 I 型干扰素信号传导而非直接病毒感染介导的,因为 IFN-β 缺陷小鼠表现出正常妊娠结局,并且尽管病毒载量较高,但阻断干扰素受体活性可改善胎盘病理。据我们所知,这些研究结果代表了 VSV-EBOV 疫苗接种 在怀孕期间的首次全面临床前安全性评估,并确定了妊娠早期脆弱性的关键窗口。更广泛地说,这项工作强调了干扰素在塑造胎盘 免疫应答 中的核心作用,并提供了一个实验框架来指导妊娠期活病毒 疫苗 的评估。

analysis_zh.main_results: 然而,围植入期 疫苗接种 适度增加胎儿吸收和产后早期 死亡率,并伴有以血管重塑缺陷和炎症为特征的胎盘病理。

papers.title: SARS, H1N1, EBOLA, COVID-19, MPOX, H5N1 AND HANTAVIRUS: IS HUMANITY ENTERING A NEW ERA OF PANDEMIC? IS TÜRKİYE PREPARED FOR THE NEXT GLOBAL OUTBREAK?
papers.abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases pose persistent challenges to global health security. Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 传染病的出现和再次出现对全球卫生安全构成持续挑战。本研究旨在检查主要传染病 暴发 并评估土耳其对未来潜在的全球 暴发 的准备情况。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 基于对科学出版物和机构报告的结构化文献检索和文档分析,采用了描述性综述设计。使用 SWOT 框架对调查结果进行组织和解释。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该分析将医疗基础设施、重症监护能力、数字医疗系统以及在 COVID-19 大流行期间获得的经验确定为潜在优势。暴发,例如严重急性呼吸系统综合症 (SARS)、甲型流感 (H1N1)、埃博拉病毒病、2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19)、mpox、甲型禽流感 (H5N1) 和汉坦病毒感染,凸显了针对新出现的传染病威胁做好有效准备的必要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 与医疗保健劳动力能力、人畜共患疾病 监测、公共卫生素养、人类、动物和环境卫生部门之间的协调以及某些生物技术产品对外部来源的依赖相关的挑战可能会限制准备工作。气候变化、环境破坏、国际旅行、移民和全球贸易被认为是可能影响传染病出现和传播的因素。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强综合 监测 和早期预警系统,通过“同一个健康”方法改善部门间协调,提高国内 疫苗 和诊断生产能力,以及扩大基于社区的公共卫生教育,可能有助于提高土耳其对未来 暴发 的准备。这些发现凸显了针对新出现的传染病威胁进行持续、多部门准备的重要性。

papers.title: Actin remodeling by human RNA virus: mechanisms and targeted intervention
papers.abstract: The actin cytoskeleton is a central dynamic network in eukaryotic cells which preserves morphology, motility, and intracellular transport. Extensive research has confirmed the importance of actin in RNA viral infection. Actin remodeling, as a core host mechanism exploited by RNA viruses, strongly affects viral replication and transmission efficiency. This article reviews the key regulatory molecules involved in actin dynamics. Based on this foundation, we focus on recent advances in the molecular mechanisms by which six representative human RNA viruses(severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2, influenza A virus, respiratory syncytial virus, dengue virus, ebola virus and human immunodeficiency virus) hijack the host actin network, revealing the actin hijacking pathways that RNA viruses tend to select. Finally, we further summarize the current status of research on antiviral compounds that target the actin signaling pathway. Given that targeting host factors offers the unique advantage of broad-spectrum antiviral activity, this strategy offers promise for overcoming drug resistance caused by high viral mutation rates. However, its clinical application still faces difficulties in balancing cytotoxicity and efficacy. This article intends to provide a conceptual framework for novel antiviral intervention approaches targeting actin.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

papers.abstract_zh: 肌动蛋白细胞骨架是真核细胞中一个核心的动态网络,负责维持细胞形态、运动性和细胞内运输。大量研究表明,肌动蛋白在RNA病毒感染中具有重要作用。肌动蛋白重塑作为RNA病毒利用的核心宿主机制,强烈影响病毒复制和传播效率。本文综述了参与肌动蛋白动态调控的关键调节分子。在此基础上,我们重点探讨了六种代表性的人类RNA病毒(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒-2、甲型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒、登革病毒、埃博拉病毒和人类免疫缺陷病毒)如何劫持宿主肌动蛋白网络,揭示RNA病毒倾向于选择的肌动蛋白劫持途径。最后,我们进一步总结了当前针对抗病毒药物化合物作用于肌动蛋白信号通路的研究现状。鉴于针对宿主因子具有独特的广谱抗病毒药物活性优势,这种策略为克服高病毒突变率导致的耐药性提供了希望。然而,其临床应用仍面临平衡细胞毒性与疗效的困难。本文旨在为针对肌动蛋白的新型抗病毒药物干预方法提供概念框架。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 靶向 宿主 因子提供了广谱 抗病毒药物 活性的独特优势,这为克服高病毒 突变 率引起的耐药性提供了希望。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 鉴于针对 宿主 因子在平衡细胞毒性和功效方面仍然面临困难,这代表了具体的证据差距。靶向肌动蛋白信号通路进行抗病毒药物干预的临床应用仍面临挑战。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 根据综述,研究、监测、诊断、治疗和政策的具体优先事项包括进一步研究RNA病毒劫持肌动蛋白的分子机制以及开发针对肌动蛋白信号通路的抗病毒药物化合物。该策略为克服高病毒突变率引起的耐药性提供了希望,但临床应用仍面临平衡细胞毒性和疗效的困难。

papers.title: Biocontainment Transport of Patients with High-Consequence Infectious Diseases: A Narrative Review and Integrated Operational Framework for Emergency Medical Systems
papers.abstract: Background: /Objectives: The transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs) links biosafety science and emergency medicine. The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic and the multinational Andes virus outbreak associated with an expedition cruise ship have renewed attention on how such patients are moved safely between the community, hospitals and high-level isolation units. This narrative review synthesises the international literature on biocontainment transport and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Methods: A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (to 10 October 2026), complemented by guidance from the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and national authorities, was conducted and reported according to the SANRA scale. Evidence was organised across seven operational domains and combined with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service. Results: Of 2432 records identified, 1485 unique records were screened. The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings concern device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain and communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, the maintenance of team readiness during periods of low activity, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification and a role-based responsibility matrix. Conclusions: Biocontainment transport is better understood as an integrated emergency system than as a device-centred intervention. The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training and quality assurance; its components require prospective evaluation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCIDs), specifically examining biocontainment practices. The central question is how emergency medical systems can safely move patients infected with human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses and related viruses, with an emphasis on operational frameworks and system integration.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus up to 10 October 2026, guided by the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and national authorities. The findings were reported according to the SANRA scale and integrated with the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The literature is dominated by aeromedical case reports, technical evaluations, and expert consensus, with few comparative studies. Recurrent findings include device integrity and air quality within transport isolators, the risk of self-contamination during doffing, heat strain, communication limits imposed by personal protective equipment, decontamination of vehicles and isolators, team readiness during low-activity periods, and the psychological burden on patients and staff. These findings are integrated into a framework comprising a four-link containment chain, a seven-phase operational workflow, a three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based responsibility matrix.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The literature lacks comparative studies and is dominated by case reports and expert consensus, which may limit the generalizability of findings. There is also a lack of prospective evaluation of the framework components, and the review notes that the operational experience of the Italian Red Cross biocontainment transport service was used to complement the evidence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The proposed framework is a structured, consensus-based reference for planning, training, and quality assurance. The components of the framework require prospective evaluation to validate their effectiveness. Additionally, the review highlights the need for further research on comparative studies and the operational challenges of biocontainment transport.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the challenges and best practices in biocontainment transport for patients with high-consequence infectious diseases, focusing on human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses. The review synthesizes international literature and integrates it into an operational framework for emergency medical systems. Key findings include recurring issues such as device integrity, self-contamination risks, heat strain, communication limitations, and psychological burdens. The framework includes a four-link containment chain, seven-phase workflow, three-tier complexity classification, and a role-based matrix. The review emphasizes the need for prospective evaluation of the framework components and highlights the lack of comparative studies in the literature. The implications suggest that biocontainment transport should be viewed as an integrated emergency system rather than a device-centered intervention.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是严重后果传染病(HCID)患者的运输,特别是检查生物防护实践。核心问题是紧急医疗系统如何安全地转移感染人类致病性正埃博拉病毒及相关病毒的患者,重点是操作框架和系统集成。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述在世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导下,对截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日的 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus 进行了结构化检索。研究结果根据 SANRA 等级进行报告,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估、专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果包括运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、热应变、个人防护设备造成的通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间的团队准备情况以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 文献缺乏比较研究,且以病例报告和专家共识为主,这可能会限制研究结果的普遍性。还缺乏对框架组成部分的前瞻性评估,审查指出,意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验被用来补充证据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 拟议的框架是一个结构化的、基于共识的规划、培训和质量保证参考。该框架的组成部分需要进行前瞻性评估以验证其有效性。此外,该审查强调需要进一步研究比较研究和生物防护运输的操作挑战。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是严重后果传染病(HCID)患者的运输,特别是检查生物防护实践。核心问题是紧急医疗系统如何安全地转移感染人类致病性正埃博拉病毒及相关病毒的患者,重点是操作框架和系统集成。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述在世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防和控制中心、美国疾病控制和预防中心以及国家当局的指导下,对截至 2026 年 10 月 10 日的 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Scopus 进行了结构化检索。研究结果根据 SANRA 等级进行报告,并结合意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 文献以航空医学病例报告、技术评估、专家共识为主,比较研究较少。反复出现的调查结果包括运输隔离器内的设备完整性和空气质量、落纱过程中的自我污染风险、热应变、个人防护设备造成的通信限制、车辆和隔离器的净化、低活动期间的团队准备情况以及患者和工作人员的心理负担。这些发现被整合到一个框架中,该框架包括四链接遏制链、七阶段操作工作流程、三层复杂性分类和基于角色的责任矩阵。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 文献缺乏比较研究,且以病例报告和专家共识为主,这可能会限制研究结果的普遍性。还缺乏对框架组成部分的前瞻性评估,审查指出,意大利红十字会生物防护运输服务的运营经验被用来补充证据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 拟议的框架是一个结构化的、基于共识的规划、培训和质量保证参考。该框架的组成部分需要进行前瞻性评估以验证其有效性。此外,该审查强调需要进一步研究比较研究和生物防护运输的操作挑战。

papers.title: An Atlas of Antiviral Therapeutic Outcomes: How Viral Biology Shapes the Reach of Treatment
papers.abstract: Antiviral inhibition does not produce a single therapeutic endpoint: some infections can be cured after finite treatment, others require durable suppression, and others remain difficult to influence because the actionable phase is brief or anatomically inaccessible. These different outcomes reflect the biological state that preserves infection or permits return, the time during which a drug-sensitive process remains causally important, the anatomical space in which consequential virus or viral material resides, and the capacity of viral populations to evolve under therapeutic pressure. Here, we examine these relationships across curable, suppressible, latent, acute, neuroinvasive, and post-acute viral infections. Comparisons among HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, CHIKV, and other systems show how persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance can determine whether antiviral activity translates into virological cure, durable suppression, recurrence control, prevention, or incomplete therapeutic control. Human challenge studies, clinical programs with discordant outcomes, and resistance studies further illustrate where mechanistic activity and therapeutic sufficiency diverge. Across these examples, antiviral outcome depends ultimately on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that determines the subsequent fate of infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how viral biology influences antiviral therapeutic outcomes, emphasizing the variability in treatment success across different viral infections. By comparing systems such as HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, and CHIKV, the authors highlight the role of persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance in determining treatment efficacy. The study suggests that antiviral outcomes depend on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that dictates the fate of infection, offering a novel framework for understanding therapeutic success. However, the analysis is based on abstract-level comparisons and lacks detailed experimental data, limiting the confidence in its conclusions. The findings have implications for the development of targeted antiviral strategies, particularly in the context of Ebola virus disease, by underscoring the importance of viral biology in treatment outcomes.

papers.source_body_en: Antiviral inhibition does not produce a single therapeutic endpoint: some infections can be cured after finite treatment, others require durable suppression, and others remain difficult to influence because the actionable phase is brief or anatomically inaccessible. papers.abstract_zh: 抗病毒药物 抑制不会产生单一的治疗终点:一些感染可以在有限的 治疗 后治愈,另一些感染需要持久抑制,而另一些感染仍然难以影响,因为可操作阶段短暂或在解剖学上难以接近。这些不同的结果反映了保持感染或允许复发的生物学状态、药物敏感过程仍然具有因果重要性的时间、相应病毒或病毒物质驻留的解剖空间以及病毒群体在治疗压力下进化的能力。在这里,我们研究了可治愈、可抑制、潜伏、急性、神经侵袭性和急性后病毒感染之间的关系。HCV、HIV-1、HBV、HSV、流感、RSV、登革热、SARS-CoV-2、埃博拉病毒、CHIKV 和其他系统之间的比较显示持久性架构、诊断时机、组织药理学、宿主 背景和耐药性如何决定 抗病毒药物 活性是否转化为病毒学治愈、持久抑制、复发控制、预防或不完全治疗控制。人类挑战研究、结果不一致的临床项目以及耐药性研究进一步说明了机械活性和治疗充分性之间的分歧。在这些例子中,抗病毒药物 的结果最终取决于 治疗 是否能够拦截决定感染后续命运的生物状态。

analysis_zh.methods: 作者对包括 埃博拉病毒 在内的各种病毒系统的 抗病毒药物 治疗结果进行了比较分析,以了解影响 治疗 疗效的因素。
analysis_zh.main_results: HCV、HIV-1、HBV、HSV、流感、RSV、登革热、SARS-CoV-2、埃博拉病毒、CHIKV 和其他系统之间的比较表明,持久性架构、诊断时机、组织药理学、宿主 背景和耐药性决定 抗病毒药物 结果。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,抗病毒药物 结果取决于 治疗 是否能够拦截决定感染命运的生物状态,为理解治疗成功提供了一个新的框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究结果强调了病毒生物学在决定 治疗 成功和失败方面的重要性,为制定针对性的 抗病毒药物 策略提供了信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于抽象水平的比较,没有提供详细的实验数据,导致其结论的可信度中等。

papers.title: Beyond long COVID: post-acute infection syndromes across Africa, a systematic review
papers.abstract: Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) have gained global attention through Long COVID, yet many pathogens most closely linked to PAIS are endemic to Africa, where evidence remains scarce; a gap with implications for health equity and global health security. We aimed to systematically review the prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors of PAIS following non-COVID infections in Africa, and to identify priorities for future research. We conducted a systematic review, searching Medline, Embase, and grey literature until 7 November 2025 for studies in Africa reporting symptoms four or more weeks after acute infection. Case reports, case series, conference abstracts, secondary research, comments, and correspondence were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data on study characteristics, symptom prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors. As substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies, results were summarised descriptively. The study was registered on the Open Science Framework. Of 1,368 records, 65 studies were included, 42 on Ebola virus disease and 19 on chikungunya, with moderate to low risk of bias. Prevalence of PAIS ranged from 17.5% to 98.6% after Ebola and 12.1% to 78.6% after chikungunya. Musculoskeletal pain, ocular complications, headache, and fatigue predominated after Ebola; arthralgia was the hallmark of post-chikungunya disease. Substantial symptom burden persisted years after acute infection. Female sex, older age, and greater acute disease severity were the factors most frequently reported to be associated with persistent sequelae. An exploratory, non-systematic supplementary search additionally identified sex-specific consequences among female survivors including menstrual irregularities and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Despite scarce, heterogeneous, and geographically concentrated evidence, the reported prevalence of persistent symptoms among survivors is high, although the absence of comparison groups in most studies complicates attribution to the infection itself. Health systems in Africa must adapt to provide long-term survivor care, embedding follow-up into existing chronic care platforms. As pathogens endemic to Africa carry pandemic potential and expand geographically, understanding their chronic consequences is both a matter of health equity and an urgent global health security priority.

It highlights the high prevalence of persistent symptoms, such as musculoskeletal pain, ocular complications, headache, and fatigue after Ebola, and arthralgia after chikungunya. The research underscores the need for long-term survivor care and identifies factors like female sex, older age, and greater acute disease severity as associated with persistent sequelae. papers.abstract_zh: 急性感染后综合症(PAIS)通过长新冠病毒引起了全球关注,但许多与 PAIS 密切相关的病原体是非洲流行的,而那里的证据仍然匮乏;这一差距对卫生公平和全球卫生安全产生影响。我们的目的是系统地回顾非洲非新冠病毒感染后 PAIS 的 患病率、临床表现和相关因素,并确定未来研究的重点。我们进行了系统回顾,检索了截至 2025 年 11 月 7 日的 Medline、Embase 和灰色文献,寻找在非洲报告急性感染后四周或更长时间出现症状的研究。病例报告、案例系列、会议摘要、二次研究、评论和信件被排除在外。两名评审员独立筛选记录并提取有关研究特征、症状 患病率、临床表现和相关因素的数据。由于研究中观察到显着的异质性,因此对结果进行了描述性总结。该研究已在开放科学框架上注册。在 1,368 条记录中,纳入了 65 项研究,其中 42 项涉及 埃博拉病毒病,19 项涉及基孔肯雅热,具有中度至低度偏倚风险。埃博拉病毒后 PAIS 的 患病率 范围为 17.5% 至 98.6%,基孔肯雅热病毒后 PAIS 范围为 12.1% 至 78.6%。埃博拉病毒感染后主要表现为肌肉骨骼疼痛、眼部并发症、头痛和疲劳;关节痛是后基孔肯雅病的标志。严重的症状负担在急性感染后持续数年。女性、年龄较大和急性疾病严重程度是最常报告的与持续性后遗症相关的因素。一项探索性的、非系统性的补充搜索还发现了女性幸存者中特定性别的后果,包括月经不调和不良妊娠结局。尽管证据稀缺、异质且地理集中,但报告的幸存者中持续症状的 患病率 很高,尽管大多数研究中缺乏对照组使感染本身的归因变得复杂。非洲的卫生系统必须适应提供长期幸存者护理,将后续行动纳入现有的慢性病护理平台。由于非洲流行的病原体具有大流行的可能性并在地理上扩大,了解其长期后果既是卫生公平问题,也是全球卫生安全的紧迫优先事项。

Search|t Updates Countries Disasters Organizations Topics Jobs Training Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA DR Congo UNICEF Democratic Republic of the Congo Humanitarian Situation Report No. 4 – Ebola Outbreak (Bundibugyo Virus), 30 September Format Situation Report Source UNICEF Posted 27 Oct 2026 Originally published 27 Oct 2026 Origin View original Attachments Download Report (PDF | 1.01 MB) HIGHLIGHTS Children continued to bear a disproportionate share of the outbreak. As of 30 September, children accounted for approximately 27 per cent of confirmed cases but nearly 38 per cent of deaths, with children under five representing almost two-thirds of child deaths. In response to the outbreak’s geographic expansion, UNICEF scaled up its multisectoral operations from 60 to 63 health zones, maintaining a presence in all 16 hotspots. Community-based surveillance was strengthened through the deployment of 3,469 additional community mobilizers. Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) activities expanded to 55 affected health zones, mobilizing 11,513 frontline and community actors, extending collaboration from 108 to 114 radio stations, and launching intensified digital engagement and rumour management. Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) interventions transitioned from initial deployment to implementation at scale. UNICEF delivered more than 590,000 litres of safe water, expanded support to health facilities and schools, strengthened decontamination capacity, and deployed assistance to newly affected areas. With the start of the school year, 167,343 children and adolescents accessed safe and adapted learning opportunities, while 158,188 unique children received school or IPC/WASH kits. UNICEF requires US$ 113.5 million for its revised six-month response plan. As of 30 September, US$ 41 million had been mobilized, leaving a US$ 72.5 million funding gap. Timely, flexible funding is urgently required to sustain outbreak control, protect children and maintain essential health including mental health and psychosocial support, nutrition, education, IPC/WASH and protection services in communities already affected by conflict, displacement and cholera. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SITUATION UPDATE Between 1 and 30 September 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported 2,050 additional confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) cases and 979 deaths. As of 30 September, cumulative confirmed cases had reached 8,300, including 4,018 deaths, corresponding to a case fatality ratio (CFR) of 48.4 per cent. The outbreak continued to expand geographically, with confirmed cases reported for the first time in Sud-Ubangi Province, bringing the number of affected provinces to seven (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, Bas-Uélé and South-Ubangi). During September, an additional three health zones reported confirmed cases, increasing the total to 63 affected health zones, representing 37.7 per cent of the country's 167 health zones. 16 health zones across North Kivu, Ituri and Haut-Uélé provinces were identified as Ebola hotspots, highlighting the scale of transmission and the need for increased prevention, surveillance and response measures. UNICEF maintained an operational presence across all 16 hotspot health zones, delivering services in support of the Ebola response. The outbreak is now the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the DRC and the second largest globally. Ituri province remains the epicentre, accounting for 75.8 per cent of all confirmed cases 6,293 cases and 2,902 deaths, followed by North Kivu 1,601 cases and 950 deaths and Haut-Uélé 346 cases and 144 deaths. Transmission also continued in Tshopo, Bas-Uélé, South Kivu and South-Ubangi. Women and girls represent approximately 53.4 per cent of reported confirmed cases. Children aged 17 years and below account for approximately 27.4 per cent of confirmed cases and 37.6 per cent of reported deaths, indicating a disproportionate mortality burden among children. Children under five bear the greatest burden, representing approximately 63.8 per cent of deaths among children aged 17 years and below. During September, 16 health workers were identified among confirmed cases reported during the month, underscoring ongoing risks to frontline responders.
